newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SingTel unit chief dismisses mobile rival.
newsitem.headline: SingTel unit chief dismisses mobile rival.

text.p: The head of former mobile phone monopoly, Singapore Telecom Mobile Pte Ltd (SingTel Mobile), on Wednesday dismissed news that its chief rival had snatched 10 percent of the market in just three weeks.

"We believe that many of these were trial users who had signed on with them (M1) as early as December last year and were attracted by various freebies and giveaways," Lung Chien Ping said in a statement.

Neil Montefiore, chief executive of MobileOne (Asia) Pte Ltd (M1), told Reuters in an interview on Monday his firm had signed more than 35,000 new mobile phone subscribers in its first three weeks of operations.
"In this first three weeks, we must be the most successful entrant into any cellular market either initial, or second, or third, or whatever," Montefiore said.

In the SingTel Mobile statement, Lung said that in a "remarkable achievement" in the same period, his company added 30,000 subscribers to its mobile phone base and 30,000 for its paging services, where it faces competition from three players -- including M1.
Singapore opened its telecommunications market on April 1, allowing competition in mobile phone and paging services.
Since news of M1's market share snatch broke on Monday, shares in SingTel Mobile's parent company, Singapore Telecommunications Ltd (SingTel), have been pummelled on the Singapore stock market.

SingTel shares hit an all-time low of Singapore $2.35 on Tuesday trade but recovered to end Wednesday at S$2.44. That was still six cents off the S$2.50 price of the firms second tranche of shares publicly offered by the Singapore government last year.
